review.why: Review GitHub Actions workflows for script injection, privileged triggers, unpinned actions and over-broad tokens, with severity-ranked findings and fixes.
review.summary: A seven-step security review of .github/workflows files. It maps trigger trust levels, hunts for untrusted ${{ }} in run steps, checks pull_request_target and workflow_run, audits permissions, SHA-pinning and secret handling, then reports a severity table with before and after YAML. It never edits files and avoids inflating severity for fork pull requests.
strengths: Explains the real mechanism (expressions are pasted into the shell before it runs) and gives the env-variable fix for each sink.
Calibrated severity guide: critical only for privileged triggers, with explicit rules against false alarms.
Reference files for injection, supply chain, permissions and report format; a fixed output template.
cautions: Reviews workflow files only; it does not run or test them.
Two reference files (triggers-and-privilege, permissions-and-tokens) were not read in this review.
Focused on GitHub-hosted Actions; other CI systems are out of scope.
